slot.brief: Series capacitor combination with dielectric slab inserted; from circuit diagram find new charge, voltage division, or energy

stem: A battery of emf $V$ remains connected to two series capacitors as shown in the figure. A dielectric completely fills $C_1$. What is the ratio of the voltage across $C_2$ to $V$?

verdicts.working: In series, both capacitors carry charge Q. With the dielectric, C₁ = 3C and C₂ = 2C, so V₂/V = (Q/2C) / [Q/(3C) + Q/(2C)] = 3/5.
issues: The figure's labels appear misplaced: K = 3 is shown beside the upper capacitor, while C₁ = C appears beside the lower one. The text specifying that the dielectric fills C₁ supports the intended calculation.

notes: figure check: Label mismatch: the lower capacitor is labelled C1 = C, while the 'C2 = 2C' label floats near the bottom wire with no capacitor next to it. The brief requires the upper capacitor to be C1 = C (with the dielectric slab, K = 3) and the lower capacitor to be C2 = 2C.; The dielectric slab is drawn floating to the left of the wires, not inside the gap of capacitor C1.
working:
$C_1'=3C,\quad C_2=2C$.
$C_{\rm eq}=\dfrac{(3C)(2C)}{3C+2C}=\dfrac{6C}{5}$.
$Q=C_{\rm eq}V=\dfrac{6CV}{5}$.
$V_2=\dfrac{Q}{C_2}=\dfrac{3V}{5}\quad\Rightarrow\quad \dfrac{V_2}{V}=\dfrac35$.

Independent check: In series, both capacitors carry charge Q. With the dielectric, C₁ = 3C and C₂ = 2C, so V₂/V = (Q/2C) / [Q/(3C) + Q/(2C)] = 3/5.
solution:
With the dielectric, $C_1=3C$ and $C_2=2C$. The series equivalent capacitance and charge are
$$C_{\rm eq}=\frac{(3C)(2C)}{3C+2C}=\frac{6C}{5},\qquad Q=C_{\rm eq}V=\frac{6CV}{5}.$$
Thus $V_2=Q/C_2=3V/5$, so $\dfrac{V_2}{V}=\boxed{\dfrac35}$.
